### 📓 Docs Drift Check
⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/CHANGELOG.md`, `packages/metadata/CHANGELOG.md`, `packages/platform-objects/CHANGELOG.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files. Nothing else in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **3** changed package(s)).

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-core/CHANGELOG.md`, `packages/metadata/CHANGELOG.md`, `packages/platform-objects/CHANGELOG.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 811b976aa3faf138db0ec1cc9bd17dca6329b94c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Review — changes needed

Head-sha: `64369bfbf80ad109fdabbd1ae40b515bb0829257`

The PR is docs-only. It amends the released `cac0f1a` entry in three CHANGELOGs (`metadata`, `metadata-core`, `platform-objects`) with the same edits in each. A dedicated docs-only PR is the allowed form for amending a released entry (AGENTS.md, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` row). Each claim was checked against the `@objectstack/metadata@18.4.0` tag (`181ad7d4`).

- **Right.**
  - The type list. `PACKAGE_SLOTTED_STORE_TYPES` at the tag (`package-slotted-store.ts:141`) is exactly `api, agent, skill, action, email_template, permission, flow, picklist, mapping, dataset, webhook`. `tool` came later, so leaving it out is correct.
  - "The refusals" instead of "the two refusals".
  - The addressed `diff` of an unattributed version answering "not found". At the tag, `MetadataManager.diff` reads `getHistoryRecord(type, name, v, address)`, which returns `null` when `historyRowAttribution(row) !== packageId`, and then throws "Version N not found".
- **must-fix M1: the legacy-row attribution edit makes the entry wrong.** It appears twice in each file: the adr-0087 marker and the "Each history row names its package" upgrade sentence. The new text says a history row written before the column "keeps a NULL `package_id` and is attributed to none", and "only a rollback to it reads its package from the restored body's `_packageId` stamp". At the tag that is not what the code does:
  - `historyRowAttribution(row)` returns `storedRowPackageId(row)` unless the column holds the `sys_metadata` mark (`database-loader.ts:298`).
  - `storedRowPackageId` takes the column when it names a package, and otherwise **parses the history row's own stored `metadata` body and returns its `_packageId` stamp** (`:2277`).
  - Nothing on the save path strips that stamp from the snapshot. `onlyBoundStampAdded` only judges whether a save is a no-op.
  - So a legacy history row whose snapshot body is stamped is read as that package's at every door: an addressed `getHistory` / `diff` lists it under that package, and a rollback takes it as that package's. Only a row whose stored body names no package is attributed to none. The text you replaced ("read as the package its stored body names (the `_packageId` stamp), else as attributed to none") was correct.
  - The rollback half is also narrower than the new text says. The restored body's stamp is read only when the version's history row is absent or attributed to none (`recorded !== undefined ? recorded : storedItemPackageId(restoredData)`, `:1859`).

  Suggested wording:
  - Upgrade sentence: "A row written before it keeps a NULL `package_id` and is read as the package its stored body names (the `_packageId` stamp), else as attributed to none; a rollback to a version attributed to none reads its package from the restored body's stamp."
  - adr-0087 marker: "no row written before it is rewritten: its `package_id` stays NULL, and it is read as the package its stored body names, else as attributed to none."

  This matches the doc that #33464 puts on `sys_metadata_history.package_id`.

A delta that changes only that text converts this to PASS.
